item.title: SpiceJet to file overdue results after exchange's suspension warning
item.description: SpiceJet has confirmed plans to reveal its overdue financial results by December 7, adhering to essential regulatory obligations. The Bombay Stock Exchange issued a warning regarding possible trading suspensions if these results are not submitted. As a result of financial hurdles, SpiceJet's market share has diminished to just 0.6% in India's domestic aviation industry.

item.title: Dinaz Vervatwala x The Economic Times
item.description: Dinaz Vervatwala established Dinaz's Fitness, a unique women's fitness studio in Hyderabad, back in 1993. Transitioning from a career as a chartered accountant, she emerged as a prominent fitness trainer and wellness coach. Dinaz advocates for a holistic view of wellness, blending mental health and sustainable practices, drawing on her personal journey after overcoming a traumatic accident that instilled in her the values of resilience and consistency.

item.title: Adani makes smart ₹3,050 crore bet to power up its metering game
item.description: Adani Energy Solutions completed the acquisition of IntelliSmart Infrastructure for Rs 3,050 crore. This deal includes acquiring 100 percent equity share capital and redeeming convertible debentures held by NIIF. IntelliSmart provides advanced metering infrastructure and smart gas meters in India. The acquisition was approved by the Competition Commission of India in October. Adani Energy Solutions is part of the Adani Group and focuses on electricity transmission and distribution.

item.title: Jindal Power gets $470 million loan for Botswana project
item.description: Jindal Power Ltd. has acquired a $470 million loan to fuel its ambitious power project in Botswana. The financing is backed by three Indian banks, alongside participation from international institutional lenders. This initiative aligns with Jindal's previous international expansion efforts and leverages Botswana's extensive coal resources, which are essential for catering to local electricity requirements.

item.title: 56% of airlines expect air travel slowdown over next 2-3 years amid rising costs: McKinsey
item.description: More than half of airlines expect a slowdown in air travel over the next two to three years, as rising jet fuel prices, higher maintenance costs and aircraft delivery delays weigh on the aviation industry, according to a McKinsey report. The report also highlights the sector's financial challenges, profitability trends and the potential role of artificial intelligence in improving operational efficiency.

item.title: Godrej Properties acquires 31 acres in Indore for new residential project amid strong demand
item.description: Godrej Properties Ltd has acquired a 31-acre land parcel in Indore for a residential development project. This acquisition will increase the company's presence in the booming Indore property market, where demand is high. The planned development is expected to have a saleable area of approximately 0.7 million square feet. Godrej Properties already has two projects in Indore at advanced stages of completion.

item.title: Kolkata-Sairang train derailment: Preliminary probe points to faulty braking system
item.description: A preliminary investigation into the Kolkata-Sairang Express derailment highlighted the malfunction of its main braking system. The BP angle cock was found in an isolated condition, preventing the brakes from engaging properly. Train crew members reported the system was functional before departure from Guwahati. The train, after addressing an earlier braking issue, failed to stop at a signal near Digaru Station.

item.title: Power transmission developers seek relief for projects hit by interconnection delays
item.description: Power transmission developers have called on the Ministry of Power to implement key changes to enhance project completion efficiency. They highlighted the necessity for automatic financial and contractual relief when delays stem from interconnected infrastructure. The Electric Power Transmission Association suggested that the Central Transmission Utility of India Ltd assume a larger role in coordination efforts.

item.title: US returns over $12 billion in oil proceeds to Venezuela since Maduro's ouster, report says
item.description: The Trump administration has reported returning over $12 billion in oil revenue to Venezuela as of September 30. Almost all funds from oil sales have been directed to support infrastructure and humanitarian needs. The U.S. Treasury managed the escrow account from which these funds were disbursed following approved requests. Various payments were made for essential supplies and services, including healthcare-related equipment.

item.title: Private power firms demand shield against project delays
item.description: In a representation to Power Secretary Pankaj Agarwal, the Electric Power Transmission Association (EPTA) has sought changes to the tariff-based competitive bidding (TBCB) framework governing inter-state transmission projects, including deemed commercial operation date, full tariff recovery and protection against penalties where a project's commissioning is held up by delays in separately awarded interconnected facilities.
